faq.a: Zakir is associated with the Arabic form ذَاكِر, whose core sense is zakir; one who remembers.

faq.q: What is the origin of Zakir?
faq.a: Zakir is associated with Arabic. Zakir is Arabic ذَاكِر (Dhākir), the active participle of ذَكَرَ, meaning 'one who remembers'.
Yes — the underlying form ذَاكِر is Arabic.
Zakir can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Zakir should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Dhākir is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Zakir mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Zakir is rendered ذاکر and carries the sense ذاکر، یاد کرنے والا.

faq.q: What does Zakir mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Zakir is rendered ذاکر and carries the sense ذاکر، یادکننده.
A romanized syllable approximation is za-kir. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Zakir?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Zakir, zakir. Script forms are ذاکر, ذَاكِر, ज़ाकिर.

faq.q: Is Zakir a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
